1. **The problem: layout work scaled with the entire document.**

   Most markdown documents previously became one `StructuredText`: `MarkdownHeadingSections.chunks` immediately returned `.plain(source)` when no collapsible headings were configured. That renderer sat inside ordinary `VStack`s, leaving no section boundaries at which SwiftUI could defer off-screen layout.

   Two related costs compounded this:

   - View evaluations recomputed the chunk split and scanned the source to choose the document width.
   - Comment and find updates changed `.id(parseVersion)`, recreating the document’s rendered subtree. Comment updates compensated by saving and asynchronously restoring the scroll offset.

   The relevant starting points are the old [`chunks`, `documentBody`, and `bumpParseVersionPreservingScroll`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift).

2. **The core implementation: make heading sections independently renderable and genuinely lazy.**

   Every recognized heading now starts a chunk, regardless of whether that heading is collapsible. Each ordinary chunk includes its heading and everything up to the next heading of **any level**. Content before the first heading becomes a separate prefix chunk.

   The other essential change is the view hierarchy. A simplified excerpt shows the arrangement:

   ```swift
   ScrollView {
       LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
           // Header, divider, and optional error view...
           ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
               chunkView(entry)
                   .bossMarkdown()
                   // Per-chunk environment and geometry modifiers...
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   The placement matters: the lazy stack is the scroll view’s document content, and `ForEach` is its direct child. Applying the theme to each chunk avoids wrapping the entire collection into one child that defeats lazy rendering. See [`MarkdownDocumentColumn.body` and `chunkView`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift).

   **Worked example — the actual large-document test fixture.** The fixture generates a title and intro, followed by 24 sections. Each section contains a paragraph, a nested list, and a fenced Swift code block. Its beginning looks like this, with the remaining sections omitted:

   ````markdown
   # Large document

   Intro paragraph with **bold** and a [link](https://example.com).

   ## Section 1

   Paragraph 1 with nested structure:

   - top
     - nested
       - deeper still, item 1

   ```swift
   let value = 1
   ```
   ````

   Relevant state: `collapsedByDefaultHeadings` is empty, comments are disabled, and the laziness test uses a **760 × 400** viewport.

   | Step | Before | After |
   |---|---|---|
   | Split source | The empty collapsible set triggers an immediate return of one `.plain(source)`. | The heading scanner finds the title plus 24 section headings, producing **25 plain chunks**. |
   | Build the document | One `StructuredText` contains all 24 sections inside eager stacks. | Each chunk can have its own `DocumentStructuredText` under the direct-child `LazyVStack`. |
   | Initial layout | There is no section-level opportunity to defer the later sections. | SwiftUI can defer off-screen sections while rendering the opening content. |
   | Observable check | The old splitter would fail the new 25-chunk assertion. | The hosting probe requires **at least one and at most 12** distinct chunks to have appeared at its observation point. |

   That last assertion is evidence of limited initial appearance, **not a measured speedup or an exact count of visible sections**. The fixture and assertions are in [`testLargeDocumentChunksAndHosts` and `testLargeDocumentLazyStackInstantiatesOnlyOnscreenChunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift).

   The useful boundary is a document without recognized ATX headings: it still becomes one chunk. This optimization therefore depends on heading structure; it does not subdivide an arbitrarily large heading-free section.

3. **The major supporting changes preserve highlighting, caching, and document presentation.**

   **Chunking and width selection are cached.** The column stores the chunks alongside the source and collapsible-heading configuration that produced them. It refreshes these on appearance and when either input changes, also caching the table-dependent document width. `documentChunks` checks those keys before returning cached data and computes a fallback if they do not match. Parser wrappers are still constructed for all chunk entries during view evaluation; the deferred work is the rendering and layout of the chunk views. See [`documentChunks`, `refreshCachedChunks`, and `renderedChunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift).

   **Highlight changes trigger parsing without changing view identity.** `StructuredText` responds to changes in its markup string, so changing the parser alone is insufficient. The new wrapper changes that string using a generation suffix:

   ```swift
   StructuredText(
       MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
       parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
   )
   ```

   Before forwarding to the actual markdown/highlight parser, the wrapper removes the suffix:

   ```swift
   func attributedString(for input: String) throws -> AttributedString {
       try inner.attributedString(for: Self.stripNonce(from: input))
   }
   ```

   For example, generation `7` appends `"\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:7-->"`. The underlying parser receives the original source, keeping highlight offsets aligned. Comment changes, flash changes, and find navigation increment the generation. Removing `.id(parseVersion)` eliminates the deliberate subtree teardown and its scroll-restoration workaround. This still requests re-parsing; it does not mutate highlights without parsing. See [`DocumentStructuredText` and `MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift).

   **Comment anchors resolve globally before being assigned locally.** Generalizing chunking creates a correctness problem: passing every comment anchor to every section could highlight repeated text in multiple sections, while a quote crossing a section boundary would exist in no individual chunk.

   The new [`MarkdownCommentAnchorMap`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift) addresses this by:

   - Projecting each chunk’s rendered markdown into plain text and concatenating those projections.
   - Resolving each anchor once against that concatenation.
   - Intersecting the resolved range with each chunk’s character range.
   - Rebuilding local `exact`, `prefix`, and `suffix` values for overlapping chunks, using up to 64 characters of surrounding context.

   The decisive clipping calculation is:

   ```swift
   let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
   let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
   guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
   ```

   Whitespace-only fragments are discarded so an isolated boundary newline cannot become an ambiguous local highlight. Flashing anchors follow the same assignment path.

   The cache separates the **plain-text projection** from **anchor assignments**. Source, heading configuration, base URL, or chunk-count changes invalidate the projection; changing comments or the flashing anchor reuses it and only recomputes assignments. Initial projection building still processes every chunk, so the change does not eliminate all document-wide parsing.

   **Search and presentation adapt to the new boundaries.** `MarkdownFindState` already searched per chunk; its changes here are documentation-only. The column now refreshes search state when collapsible-heading configuration changes. Existing match navigation and automatic expansion remain in place.

   Chunk boundaries also require explicit spacing: ordinary chunks after the first receive heading top padding, while header and divider retain explicit 12-point bottom spacing. Height preferences now come from individual chunks and reduce using `max`. Consequently, the timing logs can fire when a rendered chunk has positive height; they no longer establish that the entire document has been laid out.

4. **Tests cover the new split contract, comment correctness, and initial laziness.**

   All test changes are in [`MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift).

   | Area | Added or modified coverage |
   |---|---|
   | Heading splitting | Empty and nonmatching collapsible sets now expect separate heading chunks. Tests check exact source reconstruction, preserve fenced-code handling, and add the no-headings/single-chunk case. |
   | Highlight refresh | Checks that tagging changes the input, stripping restores the source, and generation zero leaves it unchanged. |
   | Repeated comment text | Two sections contain `checkleft run`; context selects Alpha. The test checks both assignment to exactly one chunk and actual background highlighting in exactly one parsed chunk. |
   | Cross-heading comments | Constructs a selection spanning four projected characters on either side of a boundary, then checks assignment and actual highlighting in both chunks. |
   | Whitespace fragments | Directly checks that an anchor containing only `"\n"` is rejected by `isAnchorable`. |
   | Large-document hosting | Checks 25 chunks and successful hosting with a positive fitting height. |
   | Lazy appearance | Checks that a short viewport produces some appearances without broadly instantiating the document. |

   The supporting infrastructure is small: an optional `MarkdownChunkAppearProbe` travels through the SwiftUI environment, and `DocumentStructuredText.onAppear` records its index. Production defaults to no probe. The test imports AppKit, attaches an `NSHostingView` to an `NSWindow`, and pumps the run loop until the first appearance or a two-second deadline. Its generous half-document threshold avoids depending on SwiftUI’s exact prefetch behavior.

   Coverage limits worth keeping in mind during review: the new tests do not directly assert scroll-offset preservation, cache reuse, or elapsed-time improvement. The whitespace test exercises the rejection predicate rather than the complete clipping pipeline.

   The supplied PR description reports successful Bazel builds, `BossTestsShard3`, and `checkleft run`; I have not independently rerun them.

# PR #2890: Making markdown layout lazy by heading section

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss’s markdown viewer put ordinary documents into one `StructuredText` inside eager `VStack`s. Splitting was previously enabled only for explicitly collapsible headings. Consequently, a long headed document still presented its entire rendered block tree to layout.

Highlight updates added another source of work: changing `.id(parseVersion)` recreated the document subtree. Comment updates compensated by capturing the scroll offset and restoring it on the next run-loop turn. [Base rendering and refresh path](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L423-L547).

This guide covers the complete comparison from `6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0` to `12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a`. Code links are revision-pinned source links; exact diff-location URLs were unavailable.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The fix makes **heading sections the unit of rendering and lazy layout**:

- Every recognized heading starts a chunk, whether or not any headings are collapsible.
- A direct-child `LazyVStack` exposes those chunks individually to the scroll view.
- Heading splits, document width selection, and comment-anchor projections are cached.
- Highlight changes update the markup passed to existing `StructuredText` views, instead of changing their SwiftUI identity.

Splitting also changes the scope in which comment anchors resolve. A new `MarkdownCommentAnchorMap` first selects a range across the concatenated chunk projections, then distributes that range to the overlapping chunks.

This is principally a layout optimization. Whole-document projection work still occurs, and a document without recognized headings remains one rendering chunk.

## 3. Implementation walkthrough

### Split the source into independently renderable sections

Start with [`MarkdownHeadingSections.chunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L696-L720). The decisive change removes the early return for an empty collapsible-heading set and processes **all** detected headings:

```swift
let headings = headingLines(in: source)
guard !headings.isEmpty else { return [.plain(source)] }
```

Each section ends at the next heading of **any level**. Ordinary chunks retain their heading line; collapsible chunks separate the heading label from the body passed to the parser. Any text before the first heading becomes its own plain chunk.

The existing scanner recognizes nonempty ATX headings (`#` through `######`, with required following whitespace), allows up to three leading spaces, and skips content using its existing fence-toggle logic. This is a specific source scanner, not a complete Markdown block parser. [Heading recognition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L729-L776).

### Expose those sections directly to lazy layout

The important structural change is in [`MarkdownDocumentColumn.body`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L327-L377).

Condensed structure, with styling and measurement details omitted:

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
        header
        Divider()
        if let loadError {
            loadErrorView(loadError)
        }
        ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
            chunkView(entry)
                .bossMarkdown()
        }
    }
}
```

Both placements matter: the lazy stack is the scroll view’s document content, and `ForEach` exposes individual chunks directly within it. Applying `.bossMarkdown()` per chunk avoids wrapping the entire collection in one `BossMarkdownTheme` view. The [unchanged theme implementation](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossMarkdownStyle.swift#L870-L892) confirms that this modifier introduces a wrapper.

Spacing now belongs to explicit elements: header and divider each receive 12 points below them; later plain chunks receive top padding through `MarkdownChunkTopSpacing`. In editorial mode, that modifier uses the H2 top-spacing metric for every such chunk, rather than deriving spacing from each heading’s level. Collapsible sections retain their own padding. [Chunk spacing](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L803-L828).

### Worked example: the 24-section layout fixture

Use the actual [`largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)` fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L669-L688). It contains a title and introductory paragraph, followed by 24 H2 sections, each with prose, nested list items, and a Swift code block.

Relevant state in the lazy-layout test:

```swift
let source = Self.largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)
// MarkdownDocumentChrome defaults to no collapsible headings.
commentsEnabled: false
// Hosting viewport:
NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 760, height: 400)
```

1. **Before:** the empty collapsible-heading set immediately returned `[.plain(source)]`. One `StructuredText` therefore owned the title and all 24 sections, inside the eager document stack. There was no section boundary at which the outer layout could defer rendering. [Base splitter](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L627-L653).
2. **After:** the splitter produces 25 plain chunks: title plus intro at index 0, then sections 1–24. Each becomes a separately identified child of the lazy stack. No extra prefix chunk is needed because the source starts with a heading.
3. **Observable result checked by the test:** after hosting and waiting for an appearance event, the probe must report more than zero but no more than `25 / 2`, or **12**, distinct chunk indices. This guards against broad initial appearance; it does not require an exact viewport-only count or establish a timing improvement. [Hosting test and assertions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L636-L666).

The useful boundary is heading-free prose: it still returns one `.plain(source)` chunk, so this change does not subdivide an arbitrarily large heading-free document.

### Reuse preprocessing and refresh highlights without remounting

The column stores the heading split and width selection in state. Appearance, source changes, and collapsible-heading configuration changes refresh them; ordinary body evaluations reuse the split when its source and heading keys match. There is a fallback split before the cache is current, so this is steady-state reuse, not a guarantee of exactly one scan per source. [Cache lookup and refresh](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L548-L585).

Highlight refresh uses a separate mechanism. The pinned [Textual implementation](https://github.com/gonzalezreal/textual/blob/5b06b811c0f5313b6b84bbef98c635a630638c38/Sources/Textual/StructuredText/StructuredText.swift) watches `markup` with `onChange(..., initial: true)`; swapping only the parser does not trigger parsing. `DocumentStructuredText` therefore passes:

```swift
StructuredText(
    MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
    parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
)
```

A nonzero generation appends `\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:N-->`. The wrapper strips that suffix before invoking the real parser, preserving the source seen by comment and search highlighting. [Wrapper and nonce implementation](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L783-L852).

Comment anchors, flash anchors, and find navigation increment the generation. This removes the explicit `.id()` teardown and its offset-restoration workaround; it still reparses mounted text when highlights change. Find navigation continues to expand a matching collapsed section and request an approximate scroll position. [Refresh handlers](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L385-L414).

### Preserve comment semantics across rendering boundaries

Passing every document anchor to every new chunk would highlight repeated text independently in multiple sections. A quote spanning sections could also disappear because no individual chunk contains it.

[`MarkdownCommentAnchorMap`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L93-L161) addresses both cases:

1. Project each chunk’s `renderedText` to plain text and concatenate those projections without an added separator.
2. Resolve each anchor once against that concatenation.
3. Intersect the resulting character range with each chunk.
4. Construct local anchors containing the overlapping text and up to 64 characters of local context on either side.

The decisive overlap calculation is:

```swift
let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
```

Resolution remains best-effort: the [existing resolver](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/CommentHighlightingParser.swift#L148-L193) chooses the whitespace-tolerant occurrence with the best context score, preferring the earliest tie. Local parsers then resolve the clipped anchors again. Whitespace-only fragments are explicitly rejected; this is not a new general guarantee of unambiguous anchoring.

The map’s [reference-type cache](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L28-L71) separates projection validity from highlight state. Source, heading configuration, base URL, and chunk count determine projection reuse. Changing only comments or flash state recomputes assignments without rebuilding projections.

Two related limits matter:

- Projection creation remains eager for all chunks, even with no anchors. Find state also maintains its own projected corpora.
- Find searches **within each chunk**, unlike comment resolution over concatenated projections. It does not discover a query spanning chunk boundaries. [Unchanged find computation](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Search/MarkdownFindState.swift#L169-L189).

Finally, timing now combines per-chunk heights using `max`. A positive height can trigger the existing log without waiting for every off-screen section, so `phase=parse` is no longer evidence of complete document layout. [Height preference](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L231-L237).

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added tests:**

- **Heading-free fallback:** asserts that ordinary paragraphs remain exactly one plain chunk. [Test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L317-L322).
- **Highlight nonce:** checks unchanged untagged input, changed tagged input, exact stripping, and generation-zero behavior. It exercises string helpers, not a mounted highlight update. [Test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L503-L510).
- **Comment partitioning:** repeated `checkleft run` text selects only the Alpha chunk using context; a quote built across a heading boundary assigns highlights to both chunks. Both tests run the local highlighting parsers and count chunks containing background attributes. The whitespace test only calls `isAnchorable` with `"\n"`; it does not exercise a full clipping operation. [Anchor tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L517-L610).
- **Large-document hosting and laziness:** asserts 25 chunks and positive fitting height, then separately checks the bounded appearance count described above. [Layout tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L617-L666).

**Modified/replaced tests:** the former empty-set and nonmatching-set “single plain chunk” tests now require splitting on real headings; the empty-set test also checks exact source reconstruction. The fenced-code test now expects two real-heading chunks while rejecting the fenced fake heading. Those old single-chunk expectations are replaced, not retained. Existing folding and find-index mapping tests remain. [Updated splitting assertions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L289-L322), [fence assertions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L390-L413).

**Infrastructure:** tests add an AppKit import, a generated large-document fixture, a background-attribute helper, and an environment-injected appearance probe. The lazy test hosts an `NSWindow` and pumps the run loop until the first appearance or a two-second deadline. The probe records `onAppear`, not constructor calls or layout passes.

No build/configuration files change. Existing [source globs](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L58-L64) include the new map, and the existing [Shard3 glob](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L278-L284) includes the test file.

The [PR description](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/pull/2890) reports the app-library/Shard3 build, `bazel test //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3`, and `checkleft run`. I inspected the comparison and relevant source; I did **not** run those checks. The added tests do not directly verify cache reuse, scroll preservation during highlight updates, or a measured reduction in layout time.

Documents without recognized headings still have one potentially large chunk, so the optimization’s granularity depends on document structure. ([Heading recognition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L724-L776))

### Then expose those units to SwiftUI’s lazy layout

The important hierarchy is now:

```swift
// Condensed structure; chrome and layout modifiers omitted.
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
        header
        Divider()
        if let loadError {
            loadErrorView(loadError)
        }
        ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
            chunkView(entry)
                .bossMarkdown()
        }
    }
}
```

The `LazyVStack` is the scroll content, and its `ForEach` is not hidden inside another document-body stack or conditional wrapper. Theme application also moves inside the loop. That matters because `.bossMarkdown()` returns a custom `BossMarkdownTheme` view; wrapping the entire loop would group its content behind that view boundary. ([Layout change](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L327-L379), [unchanged theme wrapper](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossMarkdownStyle.swift#L870-L892))

Spacing becomes explicit: the header and divider receive 12-point bottom padding, while later plain chunks receive heading top spacing. The latter uses the editorial H2 spacing metric for all ordinary chunk boundaries; collapsible chunks retain their own padding.

Height reporting moves to individual chunks, with preference reduction changed to `max`. Thus, a positive chunk height can trigger the existing timing logs. Those logs now indicate initial chunk layout, not completion of layout for every off-screen section.

### Worked example: the actual 24-section test fixture

**Input and state:** `largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)` generates a title heading and introductory paragraph, followed by 24 `## Section n` sections. Each contains prose, a nested list, and a fenced Swift block. The lazy-layout test uses a 760 × 400 window, disables comments, leaves the collapsible-heading set empty, and installs an appearance probe. ([Fixture and hosting test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L633-L689))

**Old behavior:**

1. The empty collapsible-heading set immediately returned `[.plain(source)]`.
2. One `StructuredText` therefore received the title, all 24 sections, and their nested content.
3. The eager document stacks offered no section-level boundary at which to defer off-screen layout. ([Base splitter](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L627-L651))

**New behavior:**

1. The splitter produces **25 plain chunks**: one title section plus 24 numbered sections. The fenced Swift content remains within its section.
2. Each chunk becomes an independently rendered child of the lazy stack.
3. Once the caches are populated, an ordinary body reevaluation with unchanged source and heading configuration reuses the split and width. Appearance, source changes, and heading-configuration changes refresh those caches; an unavailable or mismatched chunk cache falls back to computing the split. ([Cache lifecycle](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L385-L401), [cache lookup](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L571-L585))

**Observable result checked by the test:** after waiting up to two seconds for an appearance event, the probe must contain at least one chunk and no more than `25 / 2`, or **12**, distinct chunk indices:

```swift
XCTAssertGreaterThan(probe.appeared.count, 0)
XCTAssertLessThanOrEqual(probe.appeared.count, total / 2)
```

This is a regression check against broad initial appearance, not an exact visible-section count or a measured speedup. The loop stops once any appearance occurs; it does not observe the entire two-second interval. ([Assertions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L654-L666))

### Refresh highlights without recreating the document

The dependency’s `StructuredText` stores its parsed attributed string in `@State` and reparses through `.onChange(of: markup, initial: true)`. Replacing its parser instance alone does not trigger that callback. ([Pinned Textual implementation](https://github.com/gonzalezreal/textual/blob/5b06b811c0f5313b6b84bbef98c635a630638c38/Sources/Textual/StructuredText/StructuredText.swift))

The new wrapper changes the markup using `highlightGeneration`:

```swift
StructuredText(
    MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
    parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
)
```

A nonzero generation appends `\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:N-->`. The outer parser strips that suffix before invoking the comment/search parser, preserving the underlying source and its offsets. ([Wrapper and nonce parser](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L778-L854))

Comment changes, flash changes, and find navigation increment the generation. This removes the explicit `.id()` remount and its offset-restoration workaround. It still requests reparsing through each instantiated chunk’s changed markup; it does not selectively update only the chunk containing a changed highlight. Find navigation also continues to request an intentional scroll to the match.

### Preserve document-level comment selection across chunk boundaries

`MarkdownCommentAnchorMap` addresses the correctness consequence of independent parsers:

1. Project each chunk’s `renderedText` through `CommentProjection`.
2. Concatenate those projections without adding separators and record their character offsets.
3. Resolve each comment anchor once against that concatenation.
4. Intersect the resolved range with each chunk and construct local anchors for nonempty, non-whitespace fragments.

The decisive overlap calculation is:

```swift
let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
```

Clipped anchors receive local `exact` text and up to 64 characters of prefix/suffix context. Flash anchors follow the same assignment path. ([Projection and assignment](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L90-L165))

The existing resolver uses whitespace-tolerant matching, scores surrounding context when multiple candidates exist, and keeps the earliest candidate on a tie. Context is a ranking mechanism, not a required exact match. ([Unchanged resolver](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/CommentHighlightingParser.swift#L145-L190))

The map has two cache levels: source, heading configuration, base URL, and chunk count determine projection reuse; highlighted and flashing anchors additionally determine assignment reuse. A flash-only update reruns assignment without rebuilding projections. This relies on the caller deriving chunks consistently from source and heading configuration—the cache does not compare every chunk’s text. ([Cache](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L28-L69))

Find already operates on per-chunk projections, so its algorithm is unchanged. Unlike comment resolution, it searches each chunk separately; cross-boundary comment support should not be read as cross-boundary find support. Collapsible heading labels remain outside the parser/search corpus. ([Find implementation](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Search/MarkdownFindState.swift#L104-L182))

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Seven tests are added:**

| Area | Scenario and assertion |
|---|---|
| Chunking | A document without headings remains exactly one plain chunk. |
| Highlight refresh | Generation zero leaves source unchanged; generation seven changes it; stripping restores the original source. |
| Repeated comment quote | Two sections contain `checkleft run`; prefix/suffix select Alpha, only Alpha receives an anchor, and only one parsed chunk has background highlighting. |
| Cross-heading comment | An anchor derived from text on both sides of a projection boundary is assigned to both chunks; both parsed results contain highlighting. |
| Whitespace fragment | An anchor whose `exact` is `"\n"` fails `isAnchorable`. This tests the predicate directly, not end-to-end clipping. |
| Large-document hosting | The fixture produces 25 chunks and a positive hosting height. |
| Lazy layout | The short-window appearance probe records between one and 12 distinct chunks at the observation point. |

See the [no-heading test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L317-L322) and [new refresh, anchor, and layout tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L501-L689).

**Three existing behavioral tests are modified.** The empty and nonmatching collapsible-heading tests are renamed and now expect splitting at ordinary headings; the empty-set case also verifies exact source reconstruction. The fenced-code test now expects two real heading chunks, no collapsible fake heading, and exact reconstruction. The old single-chunk expectations are replaced; no separate test coverage is otherwise removed. Existing collapse-boundary and find-index mapping tests remain. ([Updated chunking tests](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L289-L322), [fence test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L387-L413))

**Infrastructure additions** are the optional environment-injected `MarkdownChunkAppearProbe`, an AppKit import, the generated large-document fixture, a helper detecting background-color attributes, and an `NSWindow`/run-loop harness for appearance delivery. The probe records `onAppear`, not parser calls or layout passes. No build configuration changes are included; existing source globs include the new production file and keep these tests in `BossTestsShard3`. ([Probe](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L237-L256), [existing Bazel configuration](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel))

The main coverage limits are direct scroll preservation during highlight changes, cache reuse/invalidation, flash-anchor behavior, and measured layout cost. The nonce test verifies string handling rather than a mounted view’s refresh lifecycle.

# PR #2890: Make markdown layout lazy without losing highlights

This guide covers base `6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0` → head `12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a`. Code links are revision-pinned.

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss’s markdown viewer put ordinary documents through one `StructuredText` inside eager `VStack`s. Heading-based splitting existed only for explicitly collapsible sections. Consequently, a long headed document still presented its entire rendered tree for layout, including content far outside the viewport.

Highlight updates compounded the cost: changing comments or find state changed `.id(parseVersion)`, recreating the document body. Comment updates attempted to preserve the viewport by capturing and asynchronously restoring its offset. See the [base rendering and remount path](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L423-L547).

The change targets repeated whole-document **layout and reconstruction**. It does not eliminate every whole-document scan or parse.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The implementation combines three changes:

- **Render heading sections independently**, making them direct children of the scroll view’s `LazyVStack`.
- **Cache source-derived work**, including the heading split, document width choice, and comment-anchor text projection.
- **Refresh highlights without changing view identity**, by changing the markup string passed to `StructuredText` and stripping the refresh marker before parsing.

Splitting also changes the scope in which comment anchors resolve. A new `MarkdownCommentAnchorMap` resolves each anchor against the concatenated chunk projections, then assigns clipped anchors to overlapping chunks. This preserves document-wide selection behavior while rendering sections separately.

The central integration point is [`MarkdownDocumentColumn`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L294-L410).

## 3. Walkthrough of the logic and architecture

### Split first, then expose the chunks to lazy layout

[`MarkdownHeadingSections.chunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L697-L720) now processes every recognized heading, even when `collapsibleHeadings` is empty:

```swift
let headings = headingLines(in: source)
guard !headings.isEmpty else { return [.plain(source)] }
```

Each section ends at the next heading of **any level**. Ordinary chunks retain their heading line; opted-in collapsible chunks separate the heading label from the body. Content preceding the first heading becomes its own plain chunk.

The unchanged scanner recognizes ATX headings and skips fenced code using the existing fence toggle. This is not a complete Markdown structural parser; for example, setext headings are not splitting boundaries. See the [heading scanner](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L730-L775).

The corresponding view hierarchy is equally important. **Condensed structure:**

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
        header
        Divider()
        // Optional error row
        ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
            chunkView(entry)
                .bossMarkdown()
                // Per-chunk environments and height reporting
        }
    }
}
```

The `ForEach` sits directly inside the lazy stack, and `.bossMarkdown()` moves onto each chunk. That modifier actually creates a [`BossMarkdownTheme` wrapper view](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossMarkdownStyle.swift#L870-L892); wrapping the entire collection would hide the individual rows behind that wrapper. See the [new layout hierarchy](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L327-L379).

Spacing becomes explicit: header and divider each get 12-point bottom padding, while subsequent plain chunks receive heading top spacing. In editorial mode that uses the H2 spacing metric, irrespective of the particular heading’s level.

### Worked example: the 24-section test document

Use the actual [`largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)` fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L669-L688): one `# Large document` heading followed by 24 `## Section …` headings, each with prose, a nested list, and fenced Swift code.

Relevant state is the default empty collapsible-heading set, comments disabled, and a 760 × 400 viewport.

| Step | Base behavior | Head behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Split source | The empty collapsible set immediately returns one `.plain(source)`. | The scanner finds 25 headings and produces 25 plain chunks. |
| Build render tree | One `StructuredText` contains the entire document under eager stacks. | Each chunk has its own `DocumentStructuredText`, exposed through the direct-child `ForEach`. |
| Initial layout | There is no section-level lazy boundary within the document. | The lazy stack can defer off-screen section views. |
| Observable check | No chunk-appearance probe exists. | The hosting test requires at least one, but at most `25 / 2 = 12`, distinct chunk indices to have appeared. |

The decisive before/after is the [old empty-set shortcut](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L627-L650) becoming [all-heading splitting](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L697-L720), combined with the lazy hierarchy above. The [hosting assertion](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L636-L666) specifies the expected observation; it is not a measured result from this review or a guarantee of an exact visible-row count.

A useful boundary: a document without recognized headings remains one chunk, so this change provides no section-level layout subdivision for it.

### Keep ordinary invalidations from repeating source-derived work

[`documentChunks` and `refreshCachedChunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L571-L585) cache the split by source and collapsible-heading configuration. Refresh runs on appearance and changes to either input; a cache mismatch can still compute a fallback split during body evaluation. The same refresh stores the table-dependent document width.

The [comment cache](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L40-L70) separates two invalidation levels:

- Source, heading set, base URL, or chunk-count changes rebuild the plain-text projection.
- Highlighted/flashing anchor changes reuse that projection and redo anchor assignment.

A completely unchanged input set returns the previous assignment. This relies on the caller deriving chunk contents from the supplied source and heading set; the cache does not compare every chunk’s contents independently.

**Work still done eagerly:** projection construction parses every chunk, even with no anchors; `MarkdownFindState.updateSource` separately builds its own chunk corpora. `renderedChunks` also rebuilds the array of parser values. The benefit is deferred rendering/layout and less repeated preprocessing, not wholly lazy document parsing. See [projection construction](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L93-L112) and [existing find-state setup](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Search/MarkdownFindState.swift#L111-L117).

### Preserve document-wide comment matching across section boundaries

The existing [`resolveRange`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/CommentHighlightingParser.swift#L146-L184) returns one whitespace-tolerant match, using prefix/suffix scores when there are multiple candidates and preferring the earliest on ties. Supplying every chunk with the original anchor list would therefore select one occurrence **per chunk**, or miss an anchor spanning chunks.

The new map concatenates the per-chunk projections without adding separators, resolves globally, and intersects the resulting character range with each chunk:

```swift
let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
let local = (overlapStart - chunkStart)..<(overlapEnd - chunkStart)
let clipped = clip(plains[index], to: local)
guard isAnchorable(clipped) else { continue }
```

[`clip`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L125-L165) creates a local `exact` plus up to 64 characters of prefix and suffix. The chunk parser then resolves that local quote again. Unresolved anchors and whitespace-only fragments are dropped.

This preserves the ordinary document’s single selected occurrence after splitting; it is not evidence that the unsplit base duplicated highlights. Search remains different: its unchanged algorithm matches within each chunk, so it does not gain cross-boundary matching from the comment map.

### Refresh highlights in place

The pinned Textual implementation watches [changes to `markup`, not changes to the parser instance](https://github.com/gonzalezreal/textual/blob/5b06b811c0f5313b6b84bbef98c635a630638c38/Sources/Textual/StructuredText/StructuredText.swift). The PR therefore replaces identity changes with a generation-tagged input:

```swift
StructuredText(
    MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
    parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
)
```

Nonzero generations append `\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:N-->`; the wrapper removes that suffix before invoking the real parser. Thus the observed markup changes while the parser receives the original source and character offsets. See [`DocumentStructuredText` and the refresh parser](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L784-L852).

Comment, flash, and find-navigation changes increment the generation. Chunk identity remains its document-order index, and the old offset capture/restore workaround disappears. Find navigation still intentionally requests scrolling and expands a matching collapsed section.

Finally, height reporting moves onto chunks and reduces with `max`. The timing callback now detects a positive chunk height; it does **not** establish that every off-screen section has parsed or laid out. See [height reduction](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L230-L235) and the [logging condition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L412-L425).

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added tests:**

- [No-heading fallback](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L315-L321): preserves one unchanged plain chunk.
- [Refresh tagging](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L503-L509): generation zero leaves source unchanged; generation seven changes it; stripping recovers the source.
- [Recurring comment quote](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L517-L548): context selects Alpha rather than Beta, and parsing the assigned anchors produces a background highlight in exactly one chunk.
- [Cross-heading anchor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L554-L606): a quote constructed across the actual projection boundary highlights both chunks. A separate test rejects a newline-only anchor through `isAnchorable`; it does not exercise the full clipping path.
- [Large-document hosting and laziness](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L617-L688): asserts 25 chunks and positive hosting height, then checks the bounded appearance count described above.

**Modified tests:** the empty and nonmatching collapsible-set tests now expect heading splitting rather than one chunk. The fenced-code test expects two real heading chunks, excludes the fenced pseudo-heading, and checks exact source reconstruction. See [split expectations](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L289-L321) and [fence coverage](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L391-L413). No standalone test scenario is removed; the two obsolete single-chunk expectations are replaced.

**Infrastructure:** the test file adds AppKit, a generated large-document fixture, and a helper detecting attributed-string background colors. A new environment-injected [`MarkdownChunkAppearProbe`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L237-L258) records distinct chunk appearances. The window-backed test pumps the run loop until an appearance occurs or two seconds elapse; it does not observe a full two-second settling period.

No build configuration changes. Existing [source globbing](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L58-L64) includes the new map, and the existing [Shard3 glob](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L278-L291) includes these tests.

The coverage establishes structural laziness and selected highlighting behavior. It does not directly assert elapsed layout cost, cache-hit counts, or viewport preservation through an actual highlight update.

# PR #2890: Make markdown layout lazy without losing highlights

This guide covers base `6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0` → head `12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a`. Code links are revision-pinned.

## 1. Problem being solved

Boss’s markdown viewer put ordinary documents through one `StructuredText` inside eager `VStack`s. Heading-based splitting existed only for explicitly collapsible sections. Consequently, a long headed document still presented its entire rendered tree for layout, including content far outside the viewport.

Highlight updates compounded the cost: changing comments or find state changed `.id(parseVersion)`, recreating the document body. Comment updates attempted to preserve the viewport by capturing and asynchronously restoring its offset. See the [base rendering and remount path](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L423-L547).

The change targets repeated whole-document **layout and reconstruction**. It does not eliminate every whole-document scan or parse.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The implementation combines three changes:

- **Render heading sections independently**, making them direct children of the scroll view’s `LazyVStack`.
- **Cache source-derived work**, including the heading split, document width choice, and comment-anchor text projection.
- **Refresh highlights without changing view identity**, by changing the markup string passed to `StructuredText` and stripping the refresh marker before parsing.

Splitting also changes the scope in which comment anchors resolve. A new `MarkdownCommentAnchorMap` resolves each anchor against the concatenated chunk projections, then assigns clipped anchors to overlapping chunks. This preserves document-wide selection behavior while rendering sections separately.

The central integration point is [`MarkdownDocumentColumn`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L294-L410).

## 3. Walkthrough of the logic and architecture

### Split first, then expose the chunks to lazy layout

[`MarkdownHeadingSections.chunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L697-L720) now processes every recognized heading, even when `collapsibleHeadings` is empty:

```swift
let headings = headingLines(in: source)
guard !headings.isEmpty else { return [.plain(source)] }
```

Each section ends at the next heading of **any level**. Ordinary chunks retain their heading line; opted-in collapsible chunks separate the heading label from the body. Content preceding the first heading becomes its own plain chunk.

The unchanged scanner recognizes ATX headings and skips fenced code using the existing fence toggle. This is not a complete Markdown structural parser; for example, setext headings are not splitting boundaries. See the [heading scanner](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L730-L775).

The corresponding view hierarchy is equally important. **Condensed structure:**

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
        header
        Divider()
        // Optional error row
        ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
            chunkView(entry)
                .bossMarkdown()
                // Per-chunk environments and height reporting
        }
    }
}
```

The `ForEach` sits directly inside the lazy stack, and `.bossMarkdown()` moves onto each chunk. That modifier actually creates a [`BossMarkdownTheme` wrapper view](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossMarkdownStyle.swift#L870-L892); wrapping the entire collection would hide the individual rows behind that wrapper. See the [new layout hierarchy](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L327-L379).

Spacing becomes explicit: header and divider each get 12-point bottom padding, while subsequent plain chunks receive heading top spacing. In editorial mode that uses the H2 spacing metric, irrespective of the particular heading’s level.

### Worked example: the 24-section test document

Use the actual [`largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)` fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L669-L688): one `# Large document` heading followed by 24 `## Section …` headings, each with prose, a nested list, and fenced Swift code.

Relevant state is the default empty collapsible-heading set, comments disabled, and a 760 × 400 viewport.

| Step | Base behavior | Head behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Split source | The empty collapsible set immediately returns one `.plain(source)`. | The scanner finds 25 headings and produces 25 plain chunks. |
| Build render tree | One `StructuredText` contains the entire document under eager stacks. | Each chunk has its own `DocumentStructuredText`, exposed through the direct-child `ForEach`. |
| Initial layout | There is no section-level lazy boundary within the document. | The lazy stack can defer off-screen section views. |
| Observable check | No chunk-appearance probe exists. | The hosting test requires at least one, but at most `25 / 2 = 12`, distinct chunk indices to have appeared. |

The decisive before/after is the [old empty-set shortcut](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L627-L650) becoming [all-heading splitting](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L697-L720), combined with the lazy hierarchy above. The [hosting assertion](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L636-L666) specifies the expected observation; it is not a measured result from this review or a guarantee of an exact visible-row count.

A useful boundary: a document without recognized headings remains one chunk, so this change provides no section-level layout subdivision for it.

### Keep ordinary invalidations from repeating source-derived work

[`documentChunks` and `refreshCachedChunks`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L571-L585) cache the split by source and collapsible-heading configuration. Refresh runs on appearance and changes to either input; a cache mismatch can still compute a fallback split during body evaluation. The same refresh stores the table-dependent document width.

The [comment cache](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L40-L70) separates two invalidation levels:

- Source, heading set, base URL, or chunk-count changes rebuild the plain-text projection.
- Highlighted/flashing anchor changes reuse that projection and redo anchor assignment.

A completely unchanged input set returns the previous assignment. This relies on the caller deriving chunk contents from the supplied source and heading set; the cache does not compare every chunk’s contents independently.

**Work still done eagerly:** projection construction parses every chunk, even with no anchors; `MarkdownFindState.updateSource` separately builds its own chunk corpora. `renderedChunks` also rebuilds the array of parser values. The benefit is deferred rendering/layout and less repeated preprocessing, not wholly lazy document parsing. See [projection construction](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L93-L112) and [existing find-state setup](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Search/MarkdownFindState.swift#L111-L117).

### Preserve document-wide comment matching across section boundaries

The existing [`resolveRange`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/CommentHighlightingParser.swift#L146-L184) returns one whitespace-tolerant match, using prefix/suffix scores when there are multiple candidates and preferring the earliest on ties. Supplying every chunk with the original anchor list would therefore select one occurrence **per chunk**, or miss an anchor spanning chunks.

The new map concatenates the per-chunk projections without adding separators, resolves globally, and intersects the resulting character range with each chunk:

```swift
let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
let local = (overlapStart - chunkStart)..<(overlapEnd - chunkStart)
let clipped = clip(plains[index], to: local)
guard isAnchorable(clipped) else { continue }
```

[`clip`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L125-L165) creates a local `exact` plus up to 64 characters of prefix and suffix. The chunk parser then resolves that local quote again. Unresolved anchors and whitespace-only fragments are dropped.

This preserves the ordinary document’s single selected occurrence after splitting; it is not evidence that the unsplit base duplicated highlights. Search remains different: its unchanged algorithm matches within each chunk, so it does not gain cross-boundary matching from the comment map.

### Refresh highlights in place

The pinned Textual implementation watches [changes to `markup`, not changes to the parser instance](https://github.com/gonzalezreal/textual/blob/5b06b811c0f5313b6b84bbef98c635a630638c38/Sources/Textual/StructuredText/StructuredText.swift). The PR therefore replaces identity changes with a generation-tagged input:

```swift
StructuredText(
    MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
    parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
)
```

Nonzero generations append `\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:N-->`; the wrapper removes that suffix before invoking the real parser. Thus the observed markup changes while the parser receives the original source and character offsets. See [`DocumentStructuredText` and the refresh parser](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L784-L852).

Comment, flash, and find-navigation changes increment the generation. Chunk identity remains its document-order index, and the old offset capture/restore workaround disappears. Find navigation still intentionally requests scrolling and expands a matching collapsed section.

Finally, height reporting moves onto chunks and reduces with `max`. The timing callback now detects a positive chunk height; it does **not** establish that every off-screen section has parsed or laid out. See [height reduction](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L230-L235) and the [logging condition](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L412-L425).

- [Recurring comment quote](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L517-L548): context selects Alpha rather than Beta, and parsing the assigned anchors produces a background highlight in exactly one chunk.
- [Cross-heading anchor](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L554-L606): a quote constructed across the actual projection boundary highlights both chunks. A separate test rejects a newline-only anchor through `isAnchorable`; it does not exercise the full clipping path.
- [Large-document hosting and laziness](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L617-L688): asserts 25 chunks and positive hosting height, then checks the bounded appearance count described above.

**Modified tests:** the empty and nonmatching collapsible-set tests now expect heading splitting rather than one chunk. The fenced-code test expects two real heading chunks, excludes the fenced pseudo-heading, and checks exact source reconstruction. See [split expectations](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L289-L321) and [fence coverage](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L391-L413). No standalone test scenario is removed; the two obsolete single-chunk expectations are replaced.

**Infrastructure:** the test file adds AppKit, a generated large-document fixture, and a helper detecting attributed-string background colors. A new environment-injected [`MarkdownChunkAppearProbe`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L237-L258) records distinct chunk appearances. The window-backed test pumps the run loop until an appearance occurs or two seconds elapse; it does not observe a full two-second settling period.

No build configuration changes. Existing [source globbing](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L58-L64) includes the new map, and the existing [Shard3 glob](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/BUILD.bazel#L278-L291) includes these tests.

The coverage establishes structural laziness and selected highlighting behavior. It does not directly assert elapsed layout cost, cache-hit counts, or viewport preservation through an actual highlight update.
